first_impression.reaction: Googled 'name change after marriage' on the train. I've got an Australian passport, I live in Singapore and we're thinking of marrying overseas. The first line tells me it's not automatic, it's dated this month, and the second paragraph goes straight to marrying overseas, which is my exact situation. Takeaways confirmed it. I jumped to the passport section and the overseas section, then the FAQ. Bookmarked.

journey.quote: A name change after marriage in Australia is a choice, and it does not happen on its own: you update each record yourself.
journey.reaction: Answer in the first sentence. Good, no scrolling through wedding fluff.

journey.quote: Marry overseas and the picture shifts. NSW and Victoria both say you will need to apply for a change of name.
journey.reaction: That's the bit I actually needed to know, and it's in the intro. Didn't expect that.

journey.quote: When the paperwork has a plan, [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=name-change-after-marriage&utm_content=primary) can take on the celebration itself.
journey.reaction: A plug before the takeaways. It's one line so I thumb past it, but it's early.

journey.quote: Agencies want the official certificate issued by the registry, not the ceremonial one signed on the day.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that. Useful, and screenshot-able.

journey.section: Your options: take, keep, hyphenate or combine
journey.quote: NSW lists three surname options that work with a marriage certificate; every other change, including moving your surname into your middle names, goes through a formal application.
journey.reaction: The heading says first or middle name, but the sentence talks about surname options. I had to read it twice to work out that a first name change means a formal application.

journey.section: How to change your name after marriage, step by step
journey.quote: Order is everything here. NSW sets out the sequence plainly: obtain your official marriage certificate, update your driver licence and Medicare card, then change your name everywhere else.
journey.reaction: Clear order, numbered steps. Easy to follow on a phone.

journey.section: Changing your name on your passport after marriage
journey.quote: As at November 2026, the Australian Passport Office says that if you change your family name because of a change in your marital status, you can choose to get a new passport or keep using your current one.
journey.reaction: Huge relief. I was worried I'd need a new passport before we fly. Dated too, so I know it's current.

journey.section: Changing your name on your passport after marriage
journey.quote: If you were born in Australia and married overseas, it will always need a name change certificate.
journey.reaction: That's me. Straight and specific, no hedging.

journey.section: State by state: NSW, Victoria, Queensland and Western Australia
journey.quote: As at November 2026, the registries agree on the broad shape but word the details differently.
journey.reaction: Long stretch of near-identical paragraphs on a small screen. I only read my state and scrolled the rest.

journey.section: Name change after an overseas or destination wedding
journey.quote: Plan for it on your return. Bring home the certificate issued where you married, and read how to [get your overseas marriage certificate](https://weddedwonderland.com/expert-advice/overseas-marriage-certificate) before you leave.
journey.reaction: Tells me what to do next and links the next thing I'd Google. I'd tap that.

journey.section: Name change after an overseas or destination wedding
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments as your single point of contact; the name change and every certificate stay with you and the official agencies.
journey.reaction: Honest that they don't do the paperwork. Since we're marrying overseas, a single contact for the venue and travel actually sounds useful.

journey.quote: It depends on your certificate and how many organisations you tell, so ask the registry for current timing when you order.
journey.reaction: The heading asks how long, and the answer mostly says ask someone else. I wanted a rough idea for the overseas route.

journey.quote: If you married in Australia, NSW says you don't need to pay the fee for an official change of name.
journey.reaction: At least I know where the costs sit: free for an Australian marriage, a registry fee if we marry overseas. Fine for now.
